comparator.name: Political Science
comparator.sourceNotes: Leiden introduced National and International Politics for students entering in 2026–27 and is phasing out the former Political Science and International Politics specialisations. The current study product and the 2026–27 programme-specific regulations define only the new route's 60-EC first year. The same regulations give second- and third-year curricula only for legacy students who entered the outgoing Political Science or International Politics specialisations by 2025–26. Combining the new first year with either legacy continuation would invent an unconfirmed entrant pathway. The published 60 EC consists of ten current credit-bearing first-year components; zero-credit mentorship, tutoring, study-advice and career-information items are omitted.
components: Politics and Policy-Making and Academic Skills 2
Law and the Rule of Law
Introduction to Statistics and Data Analysis
Politics of the European Union and Academic Skills 4

routeSelection.basis: The normalized Political Science target is separate from the normalized International Relations and Organisations target. Leiden's current official programme says 2026 entrants choose National and International Politics or International Relations and Organisations, while the former Political Science and International Politics specialisations are closed to new entrants. National and International Politics therefore represents the current broad Political Science identity for this target; the choice is independent of UCR fit.

exception.reason: Current official 2026–27 sources establish the complete 60-EC first year of the new National and International Politics route but do not publish its second- or third-year curriculum. The regulations explicitly restrict the displayed later-year Political Science and International Politics curricula to legacy cohorts admitted by 2025–26. A coherent 180-EC current-entrant comparator cannot therefore be certified without guessing how the new route will continue.
exception.curriculumContext: The supported first year covers Dutch, international, comparative and EU politics; political theory and policy-making; European history; law and the rule of law; research methods; statistics; and integrated academic skills. Leiden's transition is material rather than a minor catalogue omission: both former Dutch-taught specialisations are being phased out, and no official source currently identifies the remaining 120 EC for a 2026 entrant in National and International Politics. Revisit the comparison when Leiden publishes the route's second- and third-year requirements.
